subject: Re: CedarBridge commit structure — capped commit vs weighted ladder
messages:
From: Jason Lee <jason.lee@cedarbridge.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cedarbridge.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial commit question: per-token ladder vs capped commit

Sean —

Thanks again for the product demo last week. We’re excited about the latency profile and the caching benefits you showed. Our procurement team pulled together a short proposal (see bullets) and want to understand the concrete trade-offs. Can you confirm whether Redwood can do either of the two structures and what the practical billing differences are?

Summary of what CedarBridge is thinking:
- Committed monthly tokens: 600M tokens/month for 12 months (pilot months 1–3 at 50% ramp)
- Option A: Capped commit — fixed monthly charge that caps our spend if we exceed committed tokens (we’d still pay overage at the higher list rate but cap protects budget)
- Option B: Weighted ladder — per-token marginal breakpoints (e.g., 0–200M @ $0.0008, 200–400M @ $0.0006, 400M+ @ $0.0005) with true-up monthly

Questions:
1) How does effective blended rate compare between the two approaches for a 600M/month profile with a 50% ramp?
2) Do you support monthly true-ups or only quarterly true-ups?
3) Can you provide a simple model we can use to show CFO?

If you can send a short table + suggested SOW language for the cap we can show to finance.

Thanks —
Jason
Head of Platform
CedarBridge

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@cedarbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial commit question: per-token ladder vs capped commit

Jason —

Appreciate the clear summary. Short answers up front: we can support both Option A (capped commit) and Option B (weighted ladder). We generally do monthly true-ups for hosted API customers on usage-based deals. Below I sketched the practical differences and attached a simple model (CB-RI-PricingModel-v2.xlsx).

Quick take:
- Capped commit: predictable monthly invoice and a hard ceiling on spend. Good for finance predictability. Overages billed at list rate; you can add a safety credit band to soften spikes.
- Weighted ladder (marginal): you pay the marginal price for each token within a breakpoint — this yields lower effective blended rates on average if you consistently hit higher tiers. But month-to-month variance moves your effective bill.

Blended vs marginal example (high level):
- If you hit exactly 600M tokens and ladder is 0–200M @ $0.0008, 200–400M @ $0.0006, 400M+ @ $0.0005 -> marginal math yields: (200M*$0.0008 + 200M*$0.0006 + 200M*$0.0005)/600M = $0.000633 effective.
- Capped commit priced to give CedarBridge cost certainty; your effective rate depends on how we amortize credit and the safety band. Typically a capped commit to match the blended example above would land in the $0.00062–$0.00068 range depending on ramp and credit terms.

I've attached the model with two tabs: a monthly cadence run and a flat 12-month run. It shows a 50% ramp and both marginal and blended calculations.

Next steps:
- I’ll loop in pricing (karthik) with a suggested anchor and band we can offer.
- If you’d like a hard cap in the SOW, we can draft language (we commonly do a monthly hard cap + 1.2x buffer for safety).

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: CB-RI-PricingModel-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Thanks Sean — got the model and the example. A couple of follow-ups from our finance lead:

- We need monthly invoices with monthly true-ups (quarterly true-up won’t get approved). You indicated monthly is supported — can you confirm final billing cadence?
- For the cap option, procurement wants the mechanism: is it a hard invoice ceiling (we never pay more than X) or a credit-bank approach where you hold surplus as credit?
- We prefer a pilot structure where months 1–3 are limited to 300M tokens/month billed at the same marginal ladder but with a contractual cap so our initial spending is predictable.

If you can share SOW language and a proposed pilot amendment we’ll circulate internally.

Jason

Subject: Fwd: CedarBridge commit structure — guidance on headroom and approval

Sean / Karthik —

Looping in pricing/strategy. Quick guidance from AE side: we have ~6% discount headroom from the list rates for new mid-market pilots in this region — we can use a blended anchor to win the pilot but keep marginal breakpoints for expansion. Recommend:
- Offer pilot months 1–3 at 300M/mo with a hard monthly cap at 350M (protects CedarBridge while still allowing small spikes).
- Ladder for expansion starting month 4: 0–250M @ $0.00082, 250–500M @ $0.00058, 500M+ @ $0.00045. That gives an attractive upside as they scale.
- SOW language: define "Monthly Cap" as the invoiced amount ceiling for that billing period; overages above the cap are waived up to 10% for pilot months.

Karthik — can you run final numbers and draft the SOW amendment + one-page CFO summary? I put the HubSpot deal id HS-234789 in the doc.

Marissa
Head of Sales — East
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@cedarbridge.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CedarBridge commit structure — final numbers and two proposals

Jason — copying the formulas inline so you can paste them to CFO: (I left the model attached for line-level detail.)

Proposal 1 — Capped Commit (Pilot months 1–3)
- Committed tokens: 300M/month
- Monthly cap: invoice will not exceed $180,000 (hard cap)
- Price logic: we bill actual usage up to the cap; overages are charged at list but waived up to 10% for pilot months; surplus unused committed tokens convert to credit at the end of quarter at list rate for true-up.
- Effective blended example if usage = 300M exactly: $180,000 / 300M = $0.0006 per token effective.

Proposal 2 — Weighted Ladder (Pilot months 1–3)
- Marginal breakpoints (pilot): 0–100M @ $0.0009, 100–300M @ $0.0006
- If usage month = 300M exactly: effective blended = (100M*$0.0009 + 200M*$0.0006)/300M = $0.0007.

Notes on true-up/billing cadence:
- Monthly invoicing with monthly true-ups supported.
- We can include a contractual "Monthly Cap" clause that acts as a hard invoice ceiling for the period; overage forgiveness for pilot months is a negotiated credit (we recommend max 10% forgiveness to limit moral hazard).

Recommendation: For CedarBridge pilot, take Proposal 1 for finance predictability (hard cap) but include the ladder for month 4+ to incentivize scale. The projected blended rate over 12 months with the ramp described is ~$0.00062/token.

Attachments: SOW-draft-CedarBridge.docx (SOW with pilot cap language), CB-RI-PricingModel-v2.xlsx (detailed math).

Karthik Iyer
Lead, Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference
